results.bound: \text{NP-complete even if capacities are at most } 3
results.quote: vertex-del-sqm is NP complete even if the capacities are at most 3.

results.bound: \text{NP-hard even if each capacity is one; no }(2-\varepsilon)\text{-approximation assuming UGC for any }\varepsilon>0
results.quote: l1-min-pm is NP-hard even if each capacity is one. Furthermore, assuming the Unique Games Conjecture, it cannot be approximated within a factor of \(2-\varepsilon\) for any \(\varepsilon>0\).
l1-min-pm can be solved in polynomial time in bipartite graphs.
There is a polynomial-time 2-approximation algorithm for the l1-min-pm problem.

results.bound: \text{polynomial time in bipartite graphs; }2\text{-approximation in general graphs}
results.quote: l1-min-pmri can be solved in polynomial time in bipartite graphs, and admits a polynomial-time 2-approximation in general graphs.

results.bound: \text{NP-complete even if no woman's preference list is fixed}
results.quote: 1-forced-sm-strat and 1-forbidden-sm-strat are NP-complete even if the preference list is fixed for none of the women.
1-forced-sm-strat and 1-forbidden-sm-strat are NP-complete even if the graph is a complete bipartite graph.

results.bound: \text{NP-complete even with strict men's lists and single-tie women's lists}
results.quote: 1-forced-smti and 1-forbidden-smti are NP-complete even if each man's preference list is strict and each woman's preference list is just a single tie.
sr-strat is NP-complete even for complete graphs.

results.bound: \text{NP-complete even for complete graphs with strict or single-tie lists}
results.quote: srt is NP complete even if the graph is complete and each preference list is either strict or a single tie.

results.bound: \text{polynomial time if preferences fixed on an independent set}
results.quote: If the preferences are only fixed on an independent set, then sr-strat is polynomial-time solvable.
